avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, and the fight against emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: This year, the City is paying companies to plant and maintain trees on streets and in parks, and it is funding an organization that plants on private and institutional land. Boroughs are adding their own money, machinery and teams of employees to plant trees. Two boroughs have also allowed construction projects to depart from the rules on trees and greening.

etapes.titre: Contracts to plant trees on streets
etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees on public land, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The authorized expenditure is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, and the trees are going to seven boroughs, including Saint-Laurent (423), Verdun (281) and Pierrefonds-Roxboro (265).

etapes.titre: Money to plant on private properties
etapes.texte: The City is paying $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026. The organization and its Alliance forêt urbaine partners must plant 14,500 trees and 2,500 shrubs in 2026.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro is transferring up to $162,233.12 from its parks fund to buy trees and plants. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is renting a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75 and setting aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams, with a target of about 1,000 trees planted in 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is allowing a company to expand its building at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening, instead of the required 40 trees and 25%, with the company offsetting this on its other properties. Montréal-Nord is allowing trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

etapes.titre: Work at parc Pratt, in Outremont
etapes.texte: Outremont is awarding URBEX CONSTRUCTION INC. the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting vegetation, water retention and new pathways. The authorized expenditure is $800,416.17, taxes included, funded mainly by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit progress reports on July 31 and October 31, 2026, its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary and financial statements on March 31, 2027.
Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve's tree plantings take place from April or May to November 2026.
Watering, maintenance and replacement of trees planted under the central city's contract continue until the end of November 2029.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to clean streets, lanes, sidewalks and bike paths in the spring. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expenditure of $574,920.99, taxes included, for four vacuum sweepers and three tanker trucks [CA26 27 0008].

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is entrusting companies with the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of square Viger, place des Montréalaises and six squares including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026, to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

etapes.titre: Staff at Verdun's snow disposal site
etapes.texte: Verdun is offering city council to provide the staff for the snow disposal site itself during loading operations, for 2025, 2026 and 2027. The positions concerned are gatehouse attendants, sewer chute monitors, and drivers and operators.

Montréal-Nord approves an additional expenditure of $106,150.97, taxes included, for the rental of a grader with operator [CA26 10 086]. Saint-Léonard is drawing $200,000 from its surpluses to pay for staff and abrasives [CA26 13 0121].

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Léonard states that the adoption of its snow removal by-law is planned for September 8, 2026, with a notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026.
The extended towing contracts start on November 15, 2026.
The rental of equipment with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie resumes on November 1, 2026, and runs until March 31, 2027.
The extension of the grader rental contract in Anjou covers November 15, 2026, to April 15, 2027.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is borrowing to finance the disinfection plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant and new main pipes in the Namur–De la Savane sector. It is awarding contracts to rehabilitate water pipes using trenchless methods, rebuild streets along with their sewers and waterworks, and replace lead water service connections. It is also adding funds to projects already underway and purchasing the products and services needed to operate its plants.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes through lining, a trenchless technique, and to redo roadways and sidewalks on streets in several boroughs. These contracts also include the replacement of lead water service connections, on both the public and private sides.

The City is adding money to contracts already awarded: $200,000 in contingencies for boulevard De Maisonneuve (CA26 240015) and $1,055,231.53 for the 750 mm pipe on rue Saint-Antoine Ouest (CG26 0153). It is also adding $12,144,522.14 in contingencies for the pipe on rue de la Cathédrale, after an inspection revealed more damaged sections than in 2019 (CG26 0336).

Contracts are awarded to rebuild water pipes, sewers and roadways together, notably along rue Guy between Saint-Jacques and René-Lévesque, for a total expenditure of $28,921,033.25 (CG26 0245), and on rue De Champlain, where a 1,200 mm main pipe installed in 1927 is being replaced (CG26 0332). Other similar projects affect Saint-Laurent, Lachine, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Pierrefonds-Roxboro.

etapes.titre: Plants, wastewater treatment plant and new loan
etapes.texte: The City is renewing support for the system that controls processes at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant, extending the purchase of polymers for this plant, adding aluminum sulphate for the Pointe-Claire drinking water production plant, and extending probe-based leak detection in main pipes. It is also adopting a $12,000,000 loan to build main waterworks pipes between boulevard Cavendish and rue Isabella, in the Namur–De la Savane sector.

aSurveiller.texte: The pipe along autoroute 15 Nord and the Atwater ramp must be rehabilitated by December 18, 2026 at the latest.
Work on rue de la Cathédrale, up to the McTavish reservoir, must be completed by March 2027.
The rue Guy project must continue until December 2027.
Leak detection in main pipes must be completed by June 2028.
The ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant is expected to be put into service in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump site, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel: a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, the modernization of electrical facilities linked to biogas capture, and park maintenance. It is also requesting financial assistance from Québec for an east-west pedestrian and bike link with a footbridge. At the same time, the borough is redeveloping rue De Louvain, along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Assistance request for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is requesting up to $2,000,000 in assistance from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, including a footbridge of about 150 metres (CG26 0121). The project also includes rainwater management structures and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The agglomeration approves the construction of a research, training and community production greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then delegates the project to city council (CG26 0124). The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry it out and city council accepts (CA26 14 0039, CM26 0363).

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract of $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, which includes a new 25 kV power supply, a backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture (CG26 0223). It also entrusts two companies with the general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months (CG26 0224).

The borough entrusts Groupe MPotvin with the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $11,192,464.62. The work affects sewers and waterworks, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

The City extends by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, for an additional $296,349.21, taxes included. The compost, made from leaves collected in parks and streets, is used in particular for the landscaping of parc Frédéric-Back (CG26 0320).

The borough entrusts Les industries Harnois inc. with the supply and installation of the greenhouse complex, for a maximum amount of $499,865.92, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $574,845.80. The project involves two greenhouses with structure, envelope, natural ventilation, flooring, interior partitions and condensation water management.

aSurveiller.texte: Greenhouses: delivery of infrastructure in July 2026, work starting in August 2026 and expected completion in December 2026, according to the borough's file.
Greenhouses commissioning announced for winter 2027.
The call for projects under the ministère des Transports assistance program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Rue De Louvain: work in three phases, from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
Park maintenance: contracts from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028; 26 hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Rental of the screener and loader tractor from June 20 to October 15, 2026.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the stone walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract with Les Constructions H2D inc. to rebuild heritage walls along chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, surplus mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase; the work, 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, resumes on May 15, 2026.

The City is filing the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques area, described as covering 330 hectares, for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. Filing the application involves no expense; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan, upgrading its light fixtures to standards, and keeping the site accessible in the evening.

etapes.titre: Two areas listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The City is adding the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme area of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) to the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération, along with conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 report on land areas.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. the contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, for a total expense of $481,850.45. The work includes the new culvert, roadway resurfacing and replacement of the guardrails.

aSurveiller.texte: Expected completion of work on the chemin de Senneville stone walls: July 10, 2026.
Filing of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan: February 2027.
DarkSky International's response on the designation: April 2027.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: This year, the City is lending municipal buildings free of charge to organizations to open warming centres, and is funding organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It is also renewing a Ville-Marie public works team that carries out cleanliness interventions related to homelessness in other boroughs. In June, it set up a framework to accept private donations for housing and shelter projects.

etapes.texte: The City is lending three buildings free of charge to organizations for the 2025–2026 winter: the former church at 5600, 12e Avenue in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former Recluses Missionnaires monastery at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the former Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. All three loans end on April 30, 2026.

Verdun is paying $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers in place from January 5 to February 6, 2026, in municipal facilities and their surroundings. Ahuntsic-Cartierville confirms the continuation of COHAB inc.'s contract to operate a warming centre during the 2025–2026 winter.

etapes.titre: Funding for organizations over three years
etapes.texte: The City is granting $5,407,736 to 15 organizations and adding $3,942,461 to 10 already-funded organizations, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028. The projects deal with the inclusion of people experiencing homelessness, cohabitation in public spaces, and awareness-raising.

etapes.titre: Public works team offered to boroughs
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is offering other boroughs the services of a public works team dedicated to cleanliness related to homelessness, for 12 months starting in spring 2026, with a budget of $931,328 for 2026 coming from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and Sud-Ouest accept the offer.

Lachine, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Ahuntsic-Cartierville in turn accept the Ville-Marie team; Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles' agreement runs from May 15, 2026 to May 15, 2027. City council adopts a declaration in support of people experiencing homelessness and in recognition of the organization Maison Mobile.

The City adopts a mechanism to govern private monetary donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects for people experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless. Donors do not choose which project is funded, and the City may refuse a donation.

aSurveiller.texte: The agreement on the public works team with Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until May 15, 2027.
The financial support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs covers a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Grants, land and social, affordable or student housing projects, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: The City approves the 2026 budgets of the SHDM and the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, transfers or purchases land for social housing and pays grants to organizations that build affordable housing. It is also amending the by-law that requires developers to include social and affordable housing in their projects.

etapes.texte: City council approves the 2026 budget of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal, which manages 393 buildings and more than 5,200 affordable housing units. The urban agglomeration council approves that of the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, which houses 42,587 households.

The City obtains from the Government of Canada, at no cost, half the rights to a 3,658.8 square metre lot on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro. It also transfers, at no cost, to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni a lot at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, where 26 housing units are to be built.

The City signs two funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec for temporary housing and housing search assistance. It adds $877,312 to its assistance to Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors and grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project.

After a public consultation meeting held on February 26, 2026, city council amends the by-law on social, affordable and family housing: it will now only apply to projects larger than 18,000 square metres and will require 20% non-market housing. Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its by-law on fees for temporary occupation of public property related to social and affordable housing projects.

etapes.titre: Purchase of a lot in Le Sud-Ouest
etapes.texte: The City buys, for $9,293,113, a vacant 1,535.1 square metre lot east of rue Chatham and north of rue William, for social housing purposes. It also removes eleven lots in Ville-Marie and Le Sud-Ouest from the list of properties subject to the right of first refusal for social housing.

etapes.titre: 350 housing units at Angus, 72 housing units in Rosemont
etapes.texte: The City grants $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel to build 350 affordable housing units at the Technopôle Angus. The executive committee authorizes the SHDM to build a 72-unit building on the "Solotech" lot, on 2e Avenue.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline for the sale of the lot at rue Chatham and rue William: August 12, 2026.
SHDM project on 2e Avenue: public call for tenders in late summer or early fall 2026, construction start by the end of 2026, delivery in May 2028.
Affordable housing units at Technopôle Angus: occupancy expected by April 30, 2027 at the latest.
Construction sites announced by the SHDM: De Maisonneuve in Ville-Marie in spring 2026, Jardin des Prairies in fall 2026 and a 72-unit project at the corner of Gilford and 2e Avenue in fall 2026.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary uses.

etapes.texte: City council approved amending two leases for land south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. One serves as a parking lot for Société de transport de Montréal employee vehicles, the other as paid parking for clicknpark app members.

The City is extending the free loan of a 10,000-square-foot lot to Ville en vert for its vegetable garden, a property subsidy valued at $121,100 (CM26 0447). City council also agreed to prepare the lease itself with Îlot 84 for a 78,244-square-foot lot at the southeast corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade, at no cost.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough awarded Groupe MPotvin the contract to redevelop rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82 including taxes. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The central street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council named the new street at the heart of the Louvain eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024 by the borough and the local heritage and toponymy committee.

etapes.titre: New street, utilities and decontaminated soil
etapes.texte: The contract goes to Charex inc. to build an eco-district road with sewer, water main, roadwork, lighting and environmental soil management, for a total expenditure of $15,366,336 including taxes. The City is adding $2,007,312.15 net, from the environmental liability reserve, to remediate the soil of the former gas station on the Louvain Est lot. A one-year free lease is also being granted to the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine for sunflowers and a greenhouse.

aSurveiller.texte: The Esplanade - Louvain temporary space, at 150 rue de Louvain Ouest, is supported for the period from June 9 to December 31, 2026.
The Société de transport de Montréal parking lease starts on October 1, 2026, for three years, for up to 92 days per year.
The land loan to the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The Ville en vert vegetable garden can remain in place until December 31, 2027.
The rue de Louvain construction project between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel takes place in three phases, from May 2026 to August 2028.
Four other public spaces on the site remain to be named before the development is completed, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: The City changed collection schedules and frequencies in several boroughs, and extended contracts for food waste treatment, container collection, and container transport for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It also purchased collection bins, hired companies for hydro-excavation work with residual materials treatment, and received the 2025 residual materials management reports.

etapes.texte: The City extended by six months two contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to treat food waste, with an additional expenditure of $3,269,055.43 taxes included [CG26 0045]. It also extended by 12 months the contracts for garbage collection in front-loading and semi-underground containers, and the contract for supplying and transporting containers for the écocentre Saint-Laurent.

The executive committee changed the collection days, schedules and sectors in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30 and weekly from May 1 to October 31 [CE26 0466].

The City entered into agreements with USD Global inc., Orbis Canada ltée and Plasti-Bac inc. to supply and distribute collection bins for residents. Ahuntsic-Cartierville retained Ville en vert to inform and raise awareness among residents of eight units or fewer in the districts of Ahuntsic and Sault-au-Récollet, where the garbage collection frequency is being changed, for $230,108.67 taxes included [CA26 09 0141].

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal authorized the removal of two units in the basement of 397, boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest to set up a residual materials storage room of at least 28 m² and 32 bicycle spaces. Le Sud-Ouest lifted the requirement to set up a drop-off area on the site of the future building at 2380, rue Notre-Dame Ouest, and the executive committee approved an agreement with Tricentris, which is paying $43,773.61 for a program to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations.

The urban agglomeration council took note of the 2025 residual materials management report and the accountability report for the 2020-2025 Master Plan: 415 kg of waste per person, 48% of materials diverted from disposal, and 29 of the 49 actions completed [CG26 0311]. Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Saint-Laurent and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce filed their expenditure reports for the activities delegated to them.

aSurveiller.texte: The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until September 30, 2026.
The container collection contracts and the écocentre Saint-Laurent container contract are maintained until October 31, 2027.
The program to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until December 31, 2026 at the latest.
The hydro-excavation contracts end on December 31, 2028.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks in the Namur–De la Savane sector.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a lot
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first lot of the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The extension does not involve any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer remain the same.

The City guarantees a $2,000,000 loan from the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, a non-profit organization, to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. On the same day, city council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and management of public assets in the neighbourhood.

City council adopts a $29,000,000 loan by-law for soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, professional fees and land purchases. This work must serve the first lots of phase 1, intended for social, community and affordable housing.

A second loan by-law, for $12,000,000, funds the construction of main water mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It covers plans and specifications, soil studies, surveying, decontamination, land purchases and a first batch of work.

aSurveiller.texte: October 31, 2027: deadline set by the Québec government to sell a first lot of the site.
2031: the $128.3M federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by this date.

parcs.description: Development and redevelopment of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is having parks redone in many parts of its territory: play areas, water play features, trails, sports fields and dog parks. It is awarding design and construction contracts, adjusting contracts already underway, and paying for the decontamination of sites where parks will be developed. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is repairing structures, submitting an application for an international designation, and listing a sector in the registry of protected natural environments.

etapes.texte: The City is awarding the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of the parc Le Prévost, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56 to Verdun for soil studies before redoing the play areas of the parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, built on a former landfill.

etapes.titre: Work and protection at the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract for repairing the heritage walls along chemin de Senneville and is awarding a contract to rebuild a culvert under this same road, in the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It is submitting the application of the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and listing the Anse-à-l'Orme sector in the registry of protected natural environments.

etapes.titre: Contracts for redevelopment of neighbourhood parks
etapes.texte: The boroughs are awarding contracts to redo parks: parc à chien Lucie-Bruneau in Anjou, parc Mackenzie-King in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, parc canin Alexis-Nihon in Saint-Laurent, parc Monseigneur-Langlois in Verdun and parc Percy-Walters in Ville-Marie. Outremont is paying $150,000 to redo the play structure at the parc-école Saint-Germain.

City council is transferring a section of the former rue Eadie, measuring 810.2 m², to parc Campbell Ouest, in the Sud-Ouest. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a construction contract for the parc Denise-Morelle and is paying a supplement to the project's architects, while LaSalle is awarding the redevelopment of the parc J.O.R.-Leduc.

aSurveiller.texte: Parc des Eaux-Cachées public art competition: winner selection in October 2026, contract in December 2026, installation of the artwork in 2028.
Urban Night Sky Place application: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site compliance work in April 2032.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: final acceptance of the work expected in June 2027.
Parc Denise-Morelle: work from early August 2026 to November 2026.
Parc J.O.R.-Leduc: work from August 2026 to June 2028.
Parc Percy-Walters: work from July to November 2026, with a continuation in spring 2027.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and by-laws for commercial activities.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs are organizing the pedestrian streets for summer 2026: funding to boroughs and business development corporations, followed by by-laws that close streets to cars and regulate terraces, sales, music and signage. Temporary public squares are also being set up, and support services are being added, such as on-demand transit on avenue du Mont-Royal.

etapes.titre: Grant framework and end of a legal dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to grant subsidies to its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets in 2026, up to $425 per linear metre. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rues Beaubien Est and Boyer.

The executive committee pays $2,694,500 to six boroughs for pedestrian streets on commercial arteries. Ville-Marie and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopt their first by-laws, including the Placette CDN, open from April 1 to October 31, 2026.

Ville-Marie grants $375,500 to the Société de développement commercial du Village for rue Sainte-Catherine Est, and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension $102,045 for rue Villeray. Outremont sets aside $105,000 for avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique.

Outremont closes avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24, 2026. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce turns avenues Royal and Madison into pedestrian streets and public squares from June 1 to October 31, 2026. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal bans amplified instruments and games between 9 p.m. and 8 a.m. on the pedestrianized avenues. The City pays $40,000 to run activities on the pedestrian street Notre-Dame Ouest from July 10 to 19, 2026, and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce authorizes a commercial promotion on avenue de Monkland.

aSurveiller.texte: Activities on the pedestrian street Notre-Dame Ouest from July 10 to 19, 2026; the organization must submit its accountability report by August 31, 2026 at the latest.
Avenue de Monkland closed to traffic from August 19 at 10 p.m. to August 24 at 7 a.m., with activities from August 20 to 23, 2026.
Avenue Lacombe closed to cars from September 10 to 13, 2026.
Rue Ontario Est pedestrianized until September 18, 2026; parking meters return on September 17, 2026.
Avenue Bernard fully reopened to traffic starting September 25, 2026.
Placette CDN and avenues Royal and Madison: traffic returns after October 31, 2026, namely November 1, 2026 for the placette.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amended its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revised three by-laws, and Saint-Léonard two, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough changed the heights, uses and building coverage ratio in the sector bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increased the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa, to follow the Plan's density rules.

After the public consultation on March 25, 2026, the borough adopted a by-law covering urban planning, special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. The text authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and allows public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

Ahuntsic-Cartierville requested twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requested six more months, citing lack of staff, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

aSurveiller.texte: Mid-June 2026: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials, then hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.
June 16, 2027: deadline set by the ministry for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; Ahuntsic-Cartierville requested the same deadline.
June 17, 2027: deadline given to Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's police department (SPVM): contracts, neighbourhood stations, city council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of an officer
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a loan by-law of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

etapes.titre: Motorcycles, housekeeping, work at the cavalry building
etapes.texte: The City buys patrol motorcycles, extends housekeeping services at headquarters by 12 months, and awards a contract to replace the oil heating system at the cavalry building, at 1515 chemin Remembrance. It authorizes a second loan of an officer to the RCMP, starting March 30, 2026, with a budget of $136,260 for 2026.

etapes.titre: Meals for detainees, software, information campaign
etapes.texte: The City hires a company to prepare and deliver meals to people detained by the SPVM, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2029. It extends software maintenance for the call dispatch system by one year and receives an $8,000 federal grant for a campaign on sexual assault.

The City signs an agreement for 9 mm practice ammunition for shooting training and extends the SPVM's mail service by one year. It also hires companies for carpentry and painting work in SPVM buildings, and loans an officer to the Sûreté du Québec team on the export of stolen vehicles.

aSurveiller.texte: The work to replace the oil heating system at the cavalry building must start on April 28, 2026 and end on September 30, 2027.
The extension of software maintenance for the dispatch system runs until May 4, 2027; the City states it wants to replace this system with a new solution by the end of 2027.
The "Fèves au lard" fundraising event for neighbourhood station 46 will be held on October 23, 2026.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, station surroundings, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approved the budget and capital works program of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), then a loan by-law of the corporation. It also sold or leased land to the STM to expand métro facilities, entrusted the STM with work related to the blue line extension, and regulated work sites in the métro tunnel. It also signed a letter of non-objection for the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopted the STM's 2026 budget, balanced at $1,804,314,410 in revenues and expenditures, and the 2026-2035 capital works program. The city council gave the same direction.

The City entered into a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie for clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel, following an STM call for tenders. It also purchased, without a call for tenders, advertising space from Astral Affichage in the métro and buses for Espace pour la vie, up to $172,462.50 including taxes.

The City is leasing to the STM a 2,787 square-metre lot in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, south of rue de Louvain, as parking for vehicles of officers with a sticker, for a total rent of $49,293. The same borough modified bus waiting posts on its territory as part of the network overhaul.

The City signed an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion in parc Irma-LeVasseur, backing onto the métro ventilation station on avenue Wiseman, in Outremont. It also entrusted the STM with carrying out its municipal work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, for an expenditure of $3,808,451.29 including taxes.

etapes.titre: Décarie lot and tunnel work site
etapes.texte: Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce signed a new access agreement with the STM for a vacant 3,274.2 square-metre lot at 4636-4670, boulevard Décarie, and terminated the 2024 transitional occupancy agreement. Ville-Marie authorized the STM to drill and rehabilitate the vault of the green line tunnel, between Berri-UQAM and Saint-Laurent, 24 hours a day.

aSurveiller.texte: Drilling and rehabilitation work on the vault of the green line tunnel until July 31, 2026.
Awarding of contracts for the Pie-IX and Viau stations in August and October 2026; opening of the blue line extension stations expected in 2031.
Start of the STM parking lease on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
Work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, until December 2027.
Complete closure of rue Wilderton, for a maximum of two weeks, during the summer 2027 vacation period; bridge-tunnel reconstruction work from June 2026 to March 2028.

velo.titre: Bike: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and lanes, and the bike-sharing system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is buying bikes, docks and station parts for the BIXI system, and having new stations installed at street worksites. It is also funding the repair of existing bike paths, including the REV Lajeunesse, and is regularizing the rents for Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs, for their part, oversee the development and maintenance of their bike paths.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes an expenditure of $100,000, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives intended in particular for bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awards Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. the rental of a mini sweeper with operator for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide, for $153,395.05, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Sustainable mobility corridors in the east end
etapes.texte: City council adds $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for traffic lights, civil and electrical works and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on rue Hochelaga and rue du Havre. The contract reaches $11,399,999.99, taxes included.

City council approves a $125,167.62, taxes included, agreement with Hydro-Québec for rents from 2014 to 2025 on 19 plots of land used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, for a total rent of $46,896, taxes included, to rent about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for bike path purposes.

etapes.titre: Repair of the REV Lajeunesse and rue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of the repair of sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepts this offer as well as Ville-Marie's offer for pavement and bike path work under the 2019 Bike Plan. Outremont tables a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: For the REV Lajeunesse, the file indicates a call for tenders in May 2026, contract awards in June and work from July to August 2026.
The UCI Road World Championships are held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; sections along the route are targeted by pavement work in Ville-Marie.
The repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is scheduled at $570,000 in 2027.
The sustainable mobility corridors worksite resumes in spring 2026, for completion in spring or summer 2026.
